subject: Non-zero cM genetic map starting points

messages.author: ae2b3be3e252125b
messages.subject: Non-zero cM genetic map starting points
parts:
Hello Karl,

I have a more general question. Can you tell me why the genetic maps of some contigs sometimes have a starting point other than 0 cM? Or, point me toward a resource that explains this? Does this have to do with the difference between (a) the sum of all inter-marker distances and (b) total map distance?

I'm just wondering why shiftmap() is necessary in the first place (other than after using pullmap() to subset and re-zero a map).

Thanks a lot for your help.

Best,
Kevin

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Non-zero cM genetic map starting points
parts:
A common situation would be if considering a subset of markers drawn from a more comprehensive map.
The more-complete map might start at 0 cM, but your first marker is part-way in.

karl
